simple.meaning: נָזִיד (nâzîyd) is a Hebrew object word meaning “something boiled , i.e. soup.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 25:29. The surrounding context includes family line, prophetic witness, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָזִיד (H5138) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: נָזִיד (nâzîyd) / H5138 is traced through Genesis 25:29, Genesis 25:34, 2 Kings 4:38, 2 Kings 4:39 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H5138. nazid נָזִיד noun [masculine] thing sodden or boiled, pottage ; absolute ׳נ Gen 25:29 4 t.; construct נְזִיד 25:34 ; — a kind of boiled leguminous food, object of וַיָּ֫זֶד 25:29 (see זוּד Hiph`il ); defined 25:34 as עֲדָשִׁים נְזִיד (see עדשׁ ); object of בַּשֵּׁל 2Kin 4:38 ; boiled in a סִיר 4:39 compare 4:40 ; mentioned, apparently as a common food, Hag 2:12 . זִיזָה זִיזָא זִיז, see below I. זוז . זִיזָא see זִיזָה below I. זוז .

occurrences.englishText: Jacob boiled stew. Esau came in from the field, and he was famished.
Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew. He ate and drank, rose up, and went his way. So Esau despised his birthright.

Elisha came again to Gilgal. There was a famine in the land; and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him; and he said to his servant, “Get the large pot, and boil stew for the sons of the prophets.”
One went out into the field to gather herbs, and found a wild vine, and gathered a lap full of wild gourds from it, and came and cut them up into the pot of stew; for they didn’t recognize them.
So they poured out for the men to eat. As they were eating some of the stew, they cried out, and said, “Man of God, there is death in the pot!” And they could not eat it.
‘If someone carries holy meat in the fold of his garment, and with his fold touches bread, stew, wine, oil, or any food, will it become holy?’ ”
